bull_bear.body:
- Qualified audit opinion — auditor unable to comment on loans & advances, trade receivables and trade payables — The Basis for Qualified Opinion states that 'In the absence of appropriate evidence and underlying documents/agreements/contracts or independent report of the third party authority we are unable to comments on the appropriateness of the Loan & Advances, Trade receivables and Trade Payables.' Core balance-sheet items are therefore unverified.
- Qualified audit opinion — existence of fixed assets not verifiable (no Fixed Asset Register) — The auditor draws attention that 'in the absence of Fixed Asset Register and no physical verification report by the management / third party, we are unable to comment on the existence of the Fixed Assets.' A basic asset-control record is missing.
- Board's Report contradicts the auditor on the qualification — The Directors' Report states 'There is no qualification in the Auditors' Reports', while the statutory auditor issued a Qualified Opinion with two bases in the same Annual Report — a disclosure/control inconsistency.
- No operational turnover — business not yet operating — The MD&A states 'During the financial year under review, the Company did not record operational turnover', so the entire investment case rests on opportunities management is still evaluating rather than on a running business.
- Regulatory risk — MD&A: 'Changes in government policies, educational regulations, accreditation requirements, and compliance frameworks may impact the operating environment of the education sector.'
- Competitive risk — MD&A: 'The sector is highly competitive with the presence of established institutions, private training providers, ed-tech companies, and new market entrants.'
- Technology risk — MD&A: 'Rapid technological changes require continuous adaptation to digital learning methods and evolving learner expectations.'
- Market / demand risk — MD&A: 'Economic conditions, changing student preferences, and demand fluctuations in educational and vocational programs may influence business prospects.'
- Contested income-tax demands across multiple assessment years — The contingent-liability note (Ind AS 37) records income-tax demands raised by the department for AY 2010 through AY 2018 which the Company does not agree with and is pursuing for early disposal, plus TDS liabilities reflected in the default summary portal.
- Overdue MSME dues — The notes state 'There are Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, to whom the Company owes dues, which are outstanding for more than 45 days as at 31st March, 2026.'
- Dependence on availability of qualified and trained manpower — The Board's cautionary note names 'risks inherent in the Company's growth strategy, dependence on certain businesses, dependence on availability of qualified and trained manpower' as factors that may cause actual results to differ.

It states it aims to create value by offering quality educational and vocational services and by exploring projects that support learning, training, and employability enhancement. During the financial year under review the Company did not record operational turnover and continued to evaluate opportunities in the education and training space.

- Explore opportunities in skill development and vocational education, technology-enabled learning solutions, training and capacity-building programs, collaborative educational projects, and professional/employability-oriented courses.

outlook.body:
- Growing emphasis on employability, vocational training, digital learning and capacity building has created new opportunities for educational institutions and training service providers across the country.
- The sector is undergoing transformation driven by technology adoption, online learning platforms, government initiatives for skill enhancement, and increasing awareness regarding professional and vocational education.
- The Indian education sector offers substantial growth potential, supported by favourable demographics, increasing demand for skilled manpower, digital penetration, and policy support for vocational and higher education.
- Management remains optimistic about the long-term outlook of the education sector and intends to explore viable business opportunities aligned with the Company's objectives and capabilities.
